description: How a transcript entry is written as one JSON line, without its newline: a compact object with the members id, kind, text, date in that order (Swift's JSONEncoder wrote them in hash order, which changed from launch to launch, HK-416), strings escaped as JSONEncoder escapes them (\", \\, \/, \b \f \n \r \t, other C0 controls as lowercase \u00xx, everything else raw), and the date as Swift writes a Double: its shortest round-trip digits, exponential (d.ddde±XX) below 1e-4 or above 2^53, otherwise plain without a trailing .0. The id is written as the app passes it, uppercase (uuidString). Every date in the table is one a Date holds exactly, so the seconds the app passes are the seconds written.
function: TranscriptStore line encoding — input a transcript entry {id, kind, text, date}, expected the line's exact text
verifiedBy: DESIGN.md v1.6, v2.14; Tests/PowerUpTests/TranscriptFixtureTests.swift testTranscriptEncodeTable appends the entry through TranscriptStore.append in a temporary directory and compares the line it wrote. Rust: rust/powerup-core/tests/transcript.rs transcript_encode_cases runs transcript::entry_line.
capturedAgainst: Swift 5.9.2 JSONDecoder, JSONEncoder and CryptoKit (Xcode 15.2) on macOS 27.2, PowerUp at 0bc961f

cases.name: a plain entry
cases.reason: The canonical line: id, kind, text, date, compact.

cases.name: every kind is written by name: assistant
cases.reason: Kinds are their lowercase names.

cases.name: every kind is written by name: tool
cases.reason: Kinds are their lowercase names.

cases.name: every kind is written by name: system
cases.reason: Kinds are their lowercase names.

cases.name: every kind is written by name: error
cases.reason: Kinds are their lowercase names.

cases.name: a slash is escaped
cases.reason: JSONEncoder without .withoutEscapingSlashes writes / as \/.

cases.name: quotes and backslashes are escaped
cases.reason: The two characters that must be escaped.

cases.name: a newline is escaped

input.text:
line one
with a newline inside

cases.reason: One entry is one line, so a newline inside is \n.

cases.name: control characters are escaped

input.text: a	bc d efg

cases.reason: \t \r \b \f short, other C0 controls as lowercase \u00xx.

cases.name: DEL is raw
cases.reason: DEL is not escaped.

cases.name: non-ASCII is raw
cases.reason: CJK and emoji are written as UTF-8, not escaped.

cases.name: line and paragraph separators are raw
cases.reason: U+2028 and U+2029 are written raw, as JSONEncoder does.

cases.name: a byte order mark is raw
cases.reason: U+FEFF is written raw.

cases.name: an empty text
cases.reason: An empty text is an empty string.

cases.name: a whole-second date
cases.reason: An integral Double is written without a fraction.

cases.name: the 1970 date
cases.reason: Zero is written as 0.

cases.name: a fraction
cases.reason: A short fraction.

cases.name: a date before 1970
cases.reason: A negative date.

cases.name: a microsecond date
cases.reason: Swift's shortest round-trip digits for the Double the Date holds.

cases.name: a date above 2^53
cases.reason: Above 2^53 a Double is written in exponential form.

cases.name: a date of 1e16
cases.reason: The exponent has a sign and at least two digits.

cases.name: a date halfway between two shortest spellings
cases.reason: 5 x 2^-23 lies exactly between ...062 and ...063; Swift's description takes the even digit, where Rust's formatter rounds up (found by the differential).

cases.name: a date below 1e-4
cases.reason: Below 1e-4 a Double is written in exponential form (2^-20, which a Date holds exactly).
